newsitem.title: INDIA: India truckers agree to end strike - govt official.
newsitem.headline: India truckers agree to end strike - govt official.

text.p: India's truck owners agreed on Wednesday to end a 10-day strike that severely hit the economy following an accord reached after talks initially broke down, a senior government official said.
"The strike is over," said the Surface Transport Ministry official, who said the accord was reached around 9.45 p.m. (1615 GMT) after a breakdown of talks 15 minutes earlier.
"They agreed. We agreed. That's all," said the official.

Earlier, S.P.Singh, spokesman for the All India Motor Transport Congress (AIMTC), the truckers' union, told Reuters that the strike would continue, reversing an earlier statement that the truckers were on the verge of an agreement.

Hours before that on Wednesday, Singh said the government had agreed to the truck-owners shedding their responsibility to collect a five percent service tax and also agreed to keep a hike in insurance premiums in abeyance.
Later, Singh said the talks broke down after AIMTC officials met government officials in the Finance Ministry. He did not give reasons.

The truckers representing 2.2 million vehicles had launched the strike against the tax and the premiums, which they said were too high. The tax was proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget for the fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
